briefs.title: Buy back a vacation afternoon
briefs.question: Does quantifying time lost to laundry generate more qualified guest conversations than a service-led control?
briefs.reason: Makes opportunity cost visible without claiming a guaranteed number of hours.
briefs.concept: A vacation clock advances while the laundry task disappears from the guest itinerary.
briefs.learningCriterion: Compare qualified conversations in the same reconciled wave; attention metrics remain diagnostic.
briefs.advanceEvidence: Provenanced conversation linked to this hypothesis.

briefs.title: The last clean outfit
briefs.question: Does a specific mid-trip wardrobe emergency create more qualified conversations?
briefs.reason: Dramatizes a concrete problem rather than generic convenience.
briefs.concept: POV: the final clean outfit is used, then pickup becomes the resolution.
briefs.learningCriterion: A conversation must mention current-trip need or timing to count as qualified.

briefs.title: Pack less, rewear clean
briefs.question: Does pre-trip packing utility create demand before the laundry pile becomes urgent?
briefs.reason: Reaches a different awareness moment and value frame.
briefs.concept: Split-screen suitcase math: more outfits versus a smaller bag plus one pickup.
briefs.learningCriterion: Qualifying conversation references an upcoming or ongoing stay and pickup feasibility.

briefs.title: Three-step hotel handoff
briefs.question: Does removing process uncertainty increase qualified hotel conversations?
briefs.reason: Shows logistics instead of relying on a generic convenience claim.
briefs.concept: Bag at front desk, professional wash-and-fold, return delivery in three labeled steps.
briefs.learningCriterion: Qualifying conversation includes hotel/location and requested pickup window.

briefs.title: Make the family laundry pile vanish
briefs.question: Does showing family-scale volume outperform individual-traveler framing?
briefs.reason: Changes persona, load size and emotional relief.
briefs.concept: A realistic family laundry pile becomes neatly folded stacks through a visible service transition.
briefs.learningCriterion: Qualifying conversation includes family/group laundry and an estimated bag or load.
briefs.strategicDifference: Owns family-scale relief rather than speed.

briefs.title: Checkout countdown
briefs.question: Does a departure deadline create higher-intent conversations without an unsupported speed guarantee?
briefs.reason: Frames availability around a real deadline while keeping fulfillment conditional.
briefs.concept: A checkout countdown asks whether clean clothes are ready for the next leg of the trip.
briefs.learningCriterion: Qualifying conversation supplies departure time; availability is confirmed operationally.
briefs.advanceEvidence: Provenanced qualifying conversation plus feasible service window.
briefs.strategicDifference: Owns deadline-aware intent without guaranteed turnaround.

briefs.title: Follow the bag
briefs.question: Does making every handoff visible reduce trust objections?
briefs.reason: Targets perceived risk rather than price or speed.
briefs.concept: A labeled bag journey from handoff to folded return, with no fabricated tracking capability.
briefs.learningCriterion: Track qualified conversations that ask about handling, identity or return process.

briefs.title: Price first: US$3.25/lb
briefs.question: Does leading with documented price reduce low-fit conversations and improve qualification?
briefs.reason: Trades raw conversation volume for clearer commercial intent.
briefs.concept: A plain price card explains per-pound pricing and the documented minimum before the CTA.
briefs.learningCriterion: Compare the share of conversations that accept the minimum in the same wave; no sale inference.
briefs.strategicDifference: Owns price qualification rather than persuasion.
